exam_name: Microsoft Azure AI Cloud Developer Associate

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: When your code calls an Azure OpenAI model, which name identifies the target of the request in the endpoint path?

options.A: The display name of the Microsoft Entra tenant that issued the token
options.B: The name of the resource group that contains the resource
options.C: The Azure subscription name that owns the Azure OpenAI resource
options.D: The deployment name that you chose when you deployed the model

questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI requests are routed by deployment name, which can differ from the underlying model name. Subscriptions, resource groups and tenants identify scope, not the model deployment.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Which built-in role should an application identity receive if it only needs to call Azure OpenAI inference APIs and not manage the resource?

options.A: Cognitive Services OpenAI Contributor
options.B: Cognitive Services OpenAI User
options.C: Owner on the whole subscription
options.D: Reader on the resource group only

questions.explanation: The OpenAI User role permits inference and related data-plane calls without management rights. Owner and Contributor grant far more than needed, and Reader does not allow calling the model.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A security team wants Azure OpenAI to accept only Microsoft Entra ID tokens and reject API keys. Which resource setting achieves this?

options.A: Rotate the API keys every hour with a scheduled runbook
options.B: Place the API keys in a public storage account for auditors
options.C: Turn on the free pricing tier for the resource
options.D: Disable local (key-based) authentication on the resource

questions.explanation: Disabling local authentication forces callers to use Entra ID and makes the keys unusable. Rotating or relocating keys still leaves key-based access in place.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: How is Azure OpenAI quota for a model generally allocated?

options.A: Every deployment automatically receives unlimited capacity from a single global pool
options.B: Quota is assigned per user in Microsoft Entra ID and follows the user across subscriptions
options.C: Quota is granted per subscription, Region and model, and you split it across deployments
options.D: Quota is fixed per resource group and cannot be adjusted after it is created

questions.explanation: Quota is scoped to subscription, Region and model, and you divide it among deployments. It is neither unlimited nor per user, and increases can be requested.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: What is the main difference between a Standard deployment and a Provisioned Throughput deployment in Azure OpenAI?

options.A: Standard is available only in test subscriptions, while Provisioned is available only in production
options.B: Standard can only be used with embeddings, while Provisioned can only be used with chat models
options.C: Standard reserves dedicated capacity, while Provisioned is billed only for the tokens actually consumed
options.D: Standard bills per token consumed, while Provisioned reserves model processing capacity in PTUs for predictable throughput

questions.explanation: Standard is pay-as-you-go by tokens with shared capacity. Provisioned reserves capacity through PTUs, giving more predictable latency and throughput at a fixed cost.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A company must keep prompt and completion processing inside a defined geography such as the EU, while still using a deployment type with pooled capacity. Which option fits?

options.A: A deployment that is copied to a public GitHub repository for backup
options.B: A Global Standard deployment that may process requests in any Region
options.C: A Data Zone Standard deployment for the EU
options.D: A deployment in a Region chosen at random by the service each day

questions.explanation: Data Zone deployments keep processing within a Microsoft-defined zone such as the EU or the US, while Global deployments can route requests worldwide.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Which Azure service can enforce organizational rules such as requiring private endpoints or restricting the Regions where AI resources may be created?

options.A: Azure Advisor recommendations, which block noncompliant deployments automatically
options.B: Azure Policy
options.C: Microsoft Defender for Cloud, which acts as a deployment template engine
options.D: Azure Service Health, which rejects requests from unapproved Regions

questions.explanation: Azure Policy evaluates and can deny or audit resource configurations against rules. Advisor, Service Health and Defender provide guidance or alerts rather than governing deployments through policy definitions.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: How can a team attribute the cost of shared Azure AI resources to different projects in Cost Management?

options.A: Rename each resource after the developer who created it and read the names in the invoice
options.B: Create one Microsoft Entra tenant for each project so that invoices are separated
options.C: Apply consistent resource tags such as project or cost center and group costs by tag
options.D: Disable diagnostic logging, which forces the billing system to split costs automatically

questions.explanation: Tags let you slice spend by project or cost center in Cost Management. Renaming resources, creating tenants or disabling logs does not provide reliable attribution.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: In Azure AI Foundry, what is a project used for?

options.A: To provide a virtual network appliance that inspects outgoing traffic from apps
options.B: To group and secure the assets of one solution, such as deployments, agents and evaluations
options.C: To store the source code repository for a mobile application project
options.D: To replace the Azure subscription as the unit of billing for every AI service

questions.explanation: A Foundry project groups the assets and connections needed for a particular AI solution and supports access control around them. It does not replace subscriptions or act as a source repository.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: In a chat completions conversation, which message role carries the output of a function that your code executed on the model's request?

options.A: moderator
options.B: tool
options.C: developer
options.D: system

questions.explanation: After the model requests a tool call, your application returns the result in a message with the tool role, tied to the call ID. System and developer messages carry instructions, and moderator is not a role.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What does enabling strict structured outputs with a JSON schema in an Azure OpenAI request provide?

options.A: An increase in the maximum context window of the deployment
options.B: A guarantee that the model's response conforms to the supplied JSON schema
options.C: Automatic translation of the response into the caller's language
options.D: A guarantee that every factual statement in the response is true

questions.explanation: Structured outputs constrain generation to match the schema, which makes parsing reliable. They do not verify truthfulness or change context size.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: How does an application receive tokens incrementally as they are generated by an Azure OpenAI chat model?

options.A: Set stream to true and read the server-sent events as they arrive
options.B: Send the same request repeatedly and concatenate the partial answers
options.C: Enable a stop sequence that ends every response after a single token
options.D: Set the temperature to zero so that the response is split into small parts

questions.explanation: Setting stream to true makes the service return incremental chunks as server-sent events. Temperature and stop sequences do not stream output.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: Which request parameter limits the length of the output, including reasoning tokens, for the o-series reasoning models?

options.A: max_completion_tokens
options.B: logit_bias, which trims the response to the requested length
options.C: max_tokens, which is required by every reasoning model
options.D: top_k, which limits how many words appear in the answer

questions.explanation: Reasoning models use max_completion_tokens, which covers visible output and reasoning tokens. The older max_tokens name is not the parameter for this family.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What file format is used to supply training examples when fine-tuning a chat model in Azure OpenAI?

options.A: A compressed video file of people using the application
options.B: A PDF containing the prompts and answers as running text
options.C: JSON Lines with one messages-format conversation per line
options.D: A single Excel workbook with one sheet per conversation

questions.explanation: Chat fine-tuning uses JSONL files in which each line contains a messages array with the roles and content of one example.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What is the purpose of the seed parameter in a chat completions request?

options.A: To guarantee that two requests always return exactly the same text on every model
options.B: To set the number of tokens in the input prompt automatically
options.C: To improve reproducibility of outputs by sampling consistently, on a best-effort basis
options.D: To choose which Azure Region processes the request for compliance

questions.explanation: A seed asks the model to sample consistently so repeated calls tend to match, but determinism is only best-effort. It has no effect on Region selection or prompt length.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What does the model router in Azure AI Foundry do?

options.A: It routes network packets between two virtual networks in different Regions
options.B: It selects an underlying chat model for each prompt to balance quality and cost
options.C: It stores every prompt in a router table for later fine-tuning
options.D: It converts a chat model into an embedding model at request time

questions.explanation: The model router is a deployable model that analyzes a prompt and forwards it to a suitable underlying model, optimizing cost and quality without the application choosing each time.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: Which parameter of the text-embedding-3 models lets you produce shorter vectors to reduce storage and search cost?

options.A: dimensions
options.B: stop
options.C: temperature
options.D: n

questions.explanation: The text-embedding-3 family accepts a dimensions parameter that returns truncated embeddings. Temperature, stop and n apply to chat completion behavior.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: In the Azure AI Foundry Agent Service, how do a thread and a run relate?

options.A: A thread stores the conversation messages, and a run executes the agent against that thread to produce a response
options.B: A thread and a run are two names for the same object and can be used interchangeably
options.C: A thread is a physical server, and a run is the virtual network attached to it
options.D: A run stores the conversation messages, and a thread executes the agent against the run to produce a response

questions.explanation: Threads hold messages and state for a conversation, and each run processes the thread with an agent, possibly calling tools along the way.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: Which of the following is a built-in tool that can be attached to an agent in Azure AI Foundry Agent Service?

options.A: Network sniffer, which captures packets on the agent's subnet
options.B: Disk defragmenter, which optimizes virtual machine storage
options.C: Registry editor, which changes operating system settings
options.D: Code interpreter, which runs Python code in a sandbox

questions.explanation: Code interpreter is a built-in tool alongside options such as file search and grounding tools. The others are unrelated system utilities.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: An agent run enters the requires_action state after the model asked to call one of your functions. What should the application do next?

options.A: Wait for the service to execute the function on the client's behalf
options.B: Increase the temperature so the model no longer needs the function
options.C: Delete the thread and start a new conversation from the beginning
options.D: Run the function in your code and submit its output so the run can continue

questions.explanation: With function calling, the service pauses the run and your code must run the function and return outputs. The platform cannot run your local code for you.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: What is Semantic Kernel?

options.A: A hardware accelerator that Azure attaches to GPU virtual machines
options.B: An open-source SDK for building AI agents and plugins in languages such as C#, Python and Java
options.C: A managed database service for storing relational data with vector support only
options.D: A Linux kernel module that speeds up disk access on virtual machines

questions.explanation: Semantic Kernel is Microsoft's open-source SDK for integrating models, plugins and agent orchestration into applications across several languages.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: What is the purpose of Microsoft Agent Framework?

options.A: To provide a unified open-source framework for building and orchestrating agents
options.B: To compile agent code into firmware that runs on routers and other network devices
options.C: To manage work schedules and time-off requests for human customer support agents
options.D: To replace Microsoft Entra ID as the sign-in service used by every agent

questions.explanation: Microsoft Agent Framework brings together ideas from Semantic Kernel and AutoGen into one framework for building and orchestrating agents.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: What does the Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool let an agent in Azure AI Foundry do?

options.A: Bill the agent's usage to the customer's credit card directly
options.B: Encrypt every message between the agent and the user automatically
options.C: Compress the model's weights so the agent runs on a laptop
options.D: Connect to remote MCP servers and use the tools they expose

questions.explanation: MCP defines a standard way for models to discover and call external tools. An MCP tool lets the agent use tools hosted by remote MCP servers.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: What is a connected agent in Azure AI Foundry Agent Service?

options.A: An agent that has been linked to a Bluetooth device in a meeting room
options.B: An agent whose code is stored in a connected GitHub repository
options.C: A sub-agent that a main agent can delegate tasks to as part of a multi-agent solution
options.D: An agent that only works while the developer's laptop is connected to the internet

questions.explanation: Connected agents let a main agent hand off specific tasks to specialized agents, enabling modular multi-agent designs without custom orchestration code.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: What is the role of an indexer in Azure AI Search?

options.A: It monitors the latency of user queries and adds replicas automatically
options.B: It encrypts the search index with a customer-managed key each time a query arrives
options.C: It loads data from a supported data source into an index, optionally running enrichment
options.D: It translates incoming search queries into SQL statements for a relational database

questions.explanation: Indexers automate ingestion by crawling a data source and populating the index, and they can apply a skillset to enrich the content.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: In Azure AI Search, what is a skillset?

options.A: A set of billing rules that limits how many queries may run each minute for the tenant
options.B: A collection of virtual machine sizes that are available to each replica of the search service
options.C: A pipeline of AI enrichment steps, such as OCR or entity extraction, run during indexing
options.D: A list of team member qualifications that determines who is allowed to query the service

questions.explanation: Skillsets define enrichment skills that transform and enrich content during indexing, which is central to knowledge mining.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: What does integrated vectorization in Azure AI Search provide?

options.A: Automatic conversion of a vector index into a relational database table for reporting
options.B: Built-in chunking and embedding at index time, and vectorization of queries at search time
options.C: A physical GPU card that is permanently attached to every replica in the search service
options.D: A guarantee that every query is answered without any language model being involved at all

questions.explanation: Integrated vectorization uses skills and vectorizers so the service handles chunking and embedding for documents and queries, which reduces custom pipeline code.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: What does the semantic ranker do in Azure AI Search?

options.A: It compresses the index files in order to reduce the storage cost of each partition
options.B: It replaces the index with a graph database that stores relationships between entities
options.C: It reranks the top results with language models and can return captions and answers
options.D: It automatically deletes results that are older than a specified number of days

questions.explanation: The semantic ranker applies a secondary ranking based on meaning to improve the order of results and can extract captions and direct answers.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: How does hybrid search in Azure AI Search combine keyword and vector results into one ranking?

options.A: By merging the ranked lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
options.B: By sorting the documents alphabetically by their titles
options.C: By choosing whichever list has fewer results and discarding the other
options.D: By averaging the file sizes of the documents in both result lists

questions.explanation: Hybrid queries run keyword and vector searches in parallel and fuse their rankings with RRF so that documents ranked well by either method rise to the top.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Which field definition is used to store embeddings in an Azure AI Search index?

options.A: A field of type Edm.Boolean marked as retrievable and facetable
options.B: A field of type Edm.GeographyPoint with a scoring profile applied to it
options.C: A Collection(Edm.Single) field with a set number of dimensions and a vector search profile
options.D: A field of type Edm.String with the analyzer set to a language-specific tokenizer

questions.explanation: Vector fields are collections of single-precision floats, configured with dimensions and a vector profile that points to the algorithm settings.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: In Azure AI Search, what do replicas and partitions each add?

options.A: Both add only extra languages that the service can analyze
options.B: Replicas add storage capacity, and partitions add query throughput and availability
options.C: Both are billing categories that have no effect on performance
options.D: Replicas add query throughput and availability, and partitions add storage and indexing capacity

questions.explanation: Replicas serve queries in parallel and support high availability, while partitions spread the index across more storage and increase indexing capacity.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: Why is the Azure AI Document Intelligence layout model useful for preparing documents for RAG?

options.A: It converts the whole document into a narrated video summary for its readers
options.B: It translates scanned documents into another spoken language and reads them aloud
options.C: It extracts text, tables and headings and can output Markdown that preserves that structure
options.D: It encrypts every page of a scanned document with a different unique key before indexing

questions.explanation: Layout analysis recovers reading order, tables and headings, and Markdown output lets you chunk along the document structure instead of splitting blindly.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Which four harm categories does Azure AI Content Safety evaluate in text and images?

options.A: Spam, phishing, malware and ransomware
options.B: Latency, throughput, cost and availability
options.C: Fairness, bias, drift and accuracy
options.D: Hate, sexual, violence and self-harm

questions.explanation: Content Safety classifies content in the hate, sexual, violence and self-harm categories, each with severity levels.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: What does severity level information from Azure AI Content Safety allow you to do?

options.A: Measure how long each request takes to be processed by the service on average
options.B: Calculate the price that will be charged for each request before it is sent
options.C: Set thresholds so content is blocked or allowed depending on how severe the harm is
options.D: Decide which Azure Region should store the content after it has been analyzed

questions.explanation: Each harm category returns a severity score, and applications or filters use thresholds on that score to decide what to block, for example medium and above.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Prompt Shields in Azure AI Content Safety are designed to detect what?

options.A: Network packets that exceed the maximum transmission unit of the virtual network
options.B: Spelling mistakes that appear in the prompts typed by customers of the application
options.C: Hardware failures in the GPUs that host the deployed model in the datacenter
options.D: User prompt attacks such as jailbreaks, and indirect attacks hidden in documents

questions.explanation: Prompt Shields identify direct jailbreak attempts and indirect prompt injection embedded in external content before they influence the model.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: What does groundedness detection check?

options.A: Whether the electrical wiring of the datacenter meets safety codes
options.B: Whether the user has permission to sign in to the application
options.C: Whether a model's response is supported by the source material provided to it
options.D: Whether the response has been translated into the correct language

questions.explanation: Groundedness detection identifies ungrounded content, meaning statements not supported by the supplied sources, which helps reduce hallucinations in RAG.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: What is protected material detection used for in Azure AI Content Safety?

options.A: Encrypting protected health information at rest with a customer key
options.B: Identifying model output that matches known copyrighted text or code
options.C: Detecting when a subscription is close to its spending limit
options.D: Blocking network traffic from unapproved IP addresses

questions.explanation: Protected material detection flags generated content that matches known copyrighted text or public code so the application can block or cite it.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: What is a blocklist in Azure AI Content Safety?

options.A: A list of Azure Regions in which the Content Safety service is not currently available
options.B: A record of model deployments that failed to complete successfully during the last week
options.C: A list of users who are not allowed to sign in to the Azure portal at all
options.D: A custom list of terms you want detected and blocked in addition to the built-in categories

questions.explanation: Blocklists let you add organization-specific words or phrases, such as brand terms, so they are flagged regardless of the built-in harm categories.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Which Microsoft Responsible AI principle addresses making it clear how an AI system works, its limitations and when a person is interacting with AI?

options.A: Reliability and safety
options.B: Transparency
options.C: Inclusiveness
options.D: Accountability

questions.explanation: Transparency concerns understandability, disclosure of limitations and clarity about AI use. The other principles cover access for all, dependable operation and human responsibility for outcomes.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: What is a benefit of a user-assigned managed identity compared with a system-assigned one?

options.A: It can only be used to read files from a local disk on a virtual machine
options.B: It exists independently of any one resource and can be attached to several resources
options.C: It is deleted automatically whenever the resource that uses it is restarted
options.D: It requires a password that must be typed by the developer at each sign-in

questions.explanation: A user-assigned identity is its own Azure resource with its own lifecycle and can be shared across resources, which simplifies permission management.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: What does using a customer-managed key for an Azure AI service change?

options.A: The service stops encrypting data because the customer accepts responsibility
options.B: The service can only be accessed from a single computer
options.C: You control the encryption key in Azure Key Vault that protects the service's data at rest
options.D: The key is embedded in the source code of every client application

questions.explanation: Customer-managed keys let you own and rotate the key in Key Vault, adding control over encryption at rest on top of Microsoft-managed encryption.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: How can you send Azure OpenAI request logs and metrics to Log Analytics for querying?

options.A: Copy the logs by hand from the portal each morning into a spreadsheet
options.B: Enable a public website on the resource that shows raw logs to anyone
options.C: Install a screen recorder on the developer's workstation
options.D: Configure diagnostic settings to send the logs to a Log Analytics workspace

questions.explanation: Diagnostic settings route resource logs and metrics to Log Analytics, storage or Event Hubs, where you can analyze them with KQL.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: An Azure OpenAI call returns HTTP 429. What should the client do?

options.A: Immediately resend the request in a tight loop until it succeeds
options.B: Wait for the Retry-After duration, then retry with exponential backoff
options.C: Switch to a different Microsoft Entra tenant before retrying
options.D: Delete the deployment and recreate it with a new name

questions.explanation: A 429 means the rate limit was exceeded. Honoring Retry-After and backing off prevents further throttling, whereas immediate resends make it worse.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Under what condition does Azure OpenAI prompt caching apply automatically?

options.A: Only when the developer sets the temperature to exactly zero for the request
options.B: When a prompt of 1,024 or more tokens starts with a prefix matching a recent prompt
options.C: Only when the whole prompt contains fewer than 100 tokens in the request
options.D: Only when the request is sent from the playground in the Azure portal or Foundry

questions.explanation: Prompt caching works on long prompts, starting at 1,024 tokens, when the beginning of the prompt is identical to a recent one, lowering latency and cost for the repeated portion.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: What is Global Batch in Azure OpenAI best suited for?

options.A: Large asynchronous jobs that can wait up to a day for results, at a lower price
options.B: Interactive chat sessions that need replies in less than one second
options.C: Training a new foundation model from scratch on a private dataset
options.D: Streaming audio to a mobile application in real time with low delay

questions.explanation: Global Batch processes files of requests asynchronously with a longer completion window and discounted pricing, so it fits offline jobs and not interactive use.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Which Azure API Management policy limits how many tokens a client can consume from an Azure OpenAI backend?

options.A: The azure-openai-token-limit policy
options.B: The rewrite-uri policy, which changes the path of the request
options.C: The set-cors policy, which limits the origins that can call the API
options.D: The mock-response policy, which returns a static sample response

questions.explanation: The token limit policy enforces per-key or per-subscription token quotas at the gateway, protecting shared capacity and controlling cost.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Why do teams use Bicep or the Azure Developer CLI (azd) to provision an AI application?

options.A: Deployments become repeatable and consistent across dev, test and production
options.B: They automatically find and fix every bug in the application source code
options.C: They remove the need to have any Azure subscription or permissions at all
options.D: They make foundation models free of charge to use in every Azure Region

questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code captures resources and settings in versioned files, so environments can be created reliably and reviewed like code.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: How can Azure Container Apps help you roll out a new version of an AI service gradually?

options.A: By copying the container image to every developer's laptop
options.B: By renaming the container image with the current date and time
options.C: By using revisions and splitting traffic between the current and new revision by percentage
options.D: By turning off the current version until every user has updated their browser

questions.explanation: Container Apps revisions are immutable snapshots, and traffic splitting lets you send a small share of requests to the new revision to validate it before full rollout.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: A GitHub Actions workflow must deploy to Azure without storing a long-lived secret. Which approach is recommended?

options.A: Configure OpenID Connect with a federated credential for short-lived tokens
options.B: Email the deployment token to the team and paste it at each run
options.C: Store the subscription owner's password in a repository variable
options.D: Commit the service principal secret to the repository in a config file

questions.explanation: Workload identity federation lets GitHub authenticate to Entra ID with short-lived tokens, so no reusable secret has to be stored or rotated.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: An Azure OpenAI deployment is set to automatically update to the default model version. What is a risk of this setting for a production application?

options.A: The deployment loses all of its quota whenever a new model version is published
options.B: The deployment stops working permanently the first time that any update is released
options.C: Behavior can change when the default moves, so teams pin a specific version
options.D: The deployment becomes accessible from the public internet without authentication

questions.explanation: Auto-update follows the service's default version, which can alter outputs. Pinning a version and testing upgrades gives predictable behavior.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: How is a content filtering configuration applied to an Azure OpenAI model in production?

options.A: A content filter policy is created and associated with the model deployment
options.B: The filter is applied only to the Azure portal and not to the API
options.C: The filter is written into the subscription's billing agreement
options.D: Each end user must download and install a filter on their own device

questions.explanation: Content filter configurations are attached to deployments, so every request to that deployment is evaluated with the associated policy.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Which Azure feature helps prevent someone from accidentally deleting a critical Azure AI resource?

options.A: A resource lock of type CanNotDelete
options.B: A cost budget that emails the finance team every month
options.C: A tag with the value "important" on the resource
options.D: A diagnostic setting that sends logs to Log Analytics

questions.explanation: A CanNotDelete lock blocks deletion until the lock is removed. Budgets, logs and tags do not prevent an action.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Compared with a Standard deployment, what is a typical characteristic of a Global Standard deployment in Azure OpenAI?

options.A: Requests can only be sent from within the same virtual network as the resource
options.B: Requests are billed at a flat monthly price regardless of the volume of tokens used
options.C: Requests are always processed in the single Region where the resource was created
options.D: Requests may be processed in any Region with capacity, often with higher default quota

questions.explanation: Global deployments route traffic across Regions to use available capacity, trading strict data location control for higher availability and quota.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A finance team wants to be notified when spend on Azure AI services approaches a limit. Which feature should be used?

options.A: A network security group rule that blocks traffic at month end
options.B: A Cost Management budget with alert thresholds
options.C: A managed identity that is granted the Billing Reader role
options.D: An Azure Policy that renames resources when they get expensive

questions.explanation: Budgets track actual or forecast spend and send alerts at chosen thresholds. Policies, network rules and identities do not provide spend notifications.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: A business-critical AI app must remain available if one Azure Region has a capacity problem. Which design helps?

options.A: Deploy twice into the same Region and use the same resource group for both copies
options.B: Keep a single deployment and increase the number of tokens requested by each call
options.C: Deploy the model in a second Region and route traffic through API Management or Front Door
options.D: Turn off retries in the client so that failed requests are never repeated

questions.explanation: A second Region with gateway routing provides failover for regional issues. Two copies in the same Region share the same failure domain.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Besides Azure OpenAI models, what does the Azure AI Foundry model catalog let you do?

options.A: Download the source code of every model into a Git repository for free
options.B: Order physical servers and have them shipped to your company's office
options.C: Buy additional Azure subscriptions at a discounted rate for AI workloads
options.D: Discover and deploy models from several providers, using different deployment options

questions.explanation: The catalog lists models from Microsoft, OpenAI and other providers and lets you deploy them, for example as serverless APIs or on managed compute.

questions.domain: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
questions.question: Why do many organizations use separate resource groups or subscriptions for development, test and production AI environments?

options.A: Because Azure allows only one environment for each subscription
options.B: To isolate access, quotas and cost, and to avoid test activity affecting production
options.C: Because separate subscriptions make the models more accurate
options.D: Because Azure OpenAI cannot be deployed to more than one resource group

questions.explanation: Separating environments limits blast radius, allows different permissions and quotas, and keeps costs distinct. It does not change model accuracy.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: Which two parameters of a chat completion request discourage repetition by penalizing tokens that have already appeared?

options.A: stream and n parameters together
options.B: frequency_penalty and presence_penalty
options.C: temperature and top_p sampling values
options.D: seed and logprobs settings together

questions.explanation: Frequency penalty lowers the likelihood of tokens in proportion to how often they appeared, and presence penalty discourages any token that has appeared at all, encouraging new topics.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What does the n parameter do in a chat completions request?

options.A: It specifies how many times the request is retried after a failure
options.B: It asks the service to return several alternative completions for one prompt
options.C: It sets how many Azure Regions will process the request in parallel
options.D: It limits the number of characters in the system message

questions.explanation: The n parameter controls the number of completion choices generated for each input message, which can be useful for comparing candidates. It also multiplies output token usage.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What is the Azure OpenAI Responses API?

options.A: An API that only returns the HTTP status codes of the previous requests you sent
options.B: An API that is available exclusively for use with image generation models only
options.C: A newer API for tool-using apps with stateful conversations and reasoning model support
options.D: An API that answers billing questions asked by the finance department each month

questions.explanation: The Responses API is designed for agentic and tool-using applications, with built-in tools, stateful conversations and support for newer models.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: How can an image be supplied to a multimodal chat model such as GPT-4o?

options.C: By uploading the image to the model's training dataset before every request
options.D: By renaming the image file to end in .txt and pasting its name in the system message

questions.explanation: Multimodal chat models accept image parts within a message, with the image provided as a URL or encoded data, alongside text.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: Which type of model in Azure OpenAI converts spoken audio into text?

options.B: An embedding model such as text-embedding-3-small
options.C: A fine-tuned classification model for sentiment analysis
options.D: An image generation model such as DALL-E

questions.explanation: Whisper and the newer transcription models convert audio to text. Embedding and image models handle other modalities and tasks.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: Which Azure OpenAI capability produces new images from a text description?

options.B: An image generation model such as DALL-E or gpt-image-1
options.C: A content filter that redraws unsafe images automatically
options.D: A stop sequence that draws a border around each page

questions.explanation: Image generation models take a text prompt and create images. Embeddings represent content as vectors and filters only classify it.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What is the Realtime API in Azure OpenAI designed for?

options.A: Low-latency speech-in, speech-out conversations over WebSocket or WebRTC
options.B: Synchronizing files between two Azure storage accounts in real time
options.C: Recording the clock time when each deployment was created
options.D: Scheduling batch jobs that run once every night at midnight

questions.explanation: The Realtime API streams audio and text with minimal delay, which enables natural voice assistants that respond immediately.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What is prompt flow used for in Azure AI Foundry?

options.A: Sending bulk email campaigns based on customer segments
options.B: Building, testing and evaluating flows that link prompts, tools and code
options.C: Encrypting network traffic between two on-premises data centers
options.D: Measuring the physical airflow inside a datacenter cooling system

questions.explanation: Prompt flow provides a development tool for orchestrating prompts, models and Python tools into a flow that can be run against test data and evaluated.

questions.domain: Implement generative AI solutions
questions.question: What is model distillation in Azure OpenAI?

options.A: Using outputs from a larger model, such as stored completions, to fine-tune a smaller model for a task
options.B: Copying a deployment to a different Azure subscription
options.C: Converting a chat model into a database that stores customer records
options.D: Removing all layers from a model until it can run on a mobile phone without any training

questions.explanation: Distillation trains a smaller, cheaper model on the responses of a stronger model, so it can approach the larger model's quality on a specific task.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: How is long-term memory typically provided to an agent beyond the messages in a thread?

options.A: By storing and retrieving facts from an external store such as Azure AI Search or Azure Cosmos DB
options.B: By writing the facts in the agent's name so they are always visible
options.C: By increasing the temperature so that the model remembers older conversations better
options.D: By restarting the agent host every hour so that it reloads its previous state

questions.explanation: Threads hold conversation context, while durable memory across sessions is usually kept in an external store that the agent can query and update through tools.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: What does requiring approval for tool calls on an MCP tool achieve?

options.A: The MCP server is copied into the agent's local memory for offline use
options.B: The model is prevented from ever producing tool-call requests in its output
options.C: A person must approve a tool call before the agent runs it, adding human oversight
options.D: The tool calls run faster because they are skipped by the safety layer

questions.explanation: Approval settings pause execution so a human can review and permit a tool call, which is important for actions with side effects.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: Which type of measure do Foundry evaluations for agents commonly include?

options.A: Office attendance, meeting length and vacation days
options.B: CPU temperature, disk size and memory clock speed
options.C: Screen resolution, color depth and font size
options.D: Intent resolution, tool call accuracy and task adherence

questions.explanation: Agent evaluators assess whether the agent understood the goal, called the right tools with the right arguments and followed instructions, alongside quality and safety measures.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: Which of the following is a common multi-agent orchestration pattern?

options.A: Cold storage, where agents are archived after their first response
options.B: Sequential, where agents work one after another on the previous output
options.C: Circular saw, where agents cut requests into pieces of equal size
options.D: Dial-up, where agents connect to each other using telephone lines

questions.explanation: Sequential, concurrent, group chat and handoff are common patterns for coordinating agents. The other options are not orchestration patterns.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: Which agent tool lets an agent ground its answers in a private index of company documents?

options.A: The screen capture tool
options.B: The calculator tool that cannot access external data
options.C: The clipboard tool
options.D: The Azure AI Search tool

questions.explanation: The Azure AI Search tool lets an agent query an existing index, so responses can draw on organization data rather than only the model's training.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: What does the file search tool do for an agent in Azure AI Foundry Agent Service?

options.A: It renames uploaded files to match the agent's instructions
options.B: It deletes files that the agent has not opened for a week
options.C: It lets the agent search uploaded files through a vector store the service manages
options.D: It searches the local file system of the developer's laptop for viruses

questions.explanation: File search creates and queries a vector store from uploaded documents, giving the agent retrieval over those files without building a separate pipeline.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: How can an agent call an existing REST service that is described by an OpenAPI specification?

options.A: By copying the service's source code into the agent's system message
options.B: By exporting the service to a spreadsheet and uploading the sheet
options.C: By adding an OpenAPI tool configured with the specification and an authentication method
options.D: By asking the model to guess the URLs of the operations from its training data

questions.explanation: An OpenAPI tool exposes the operations in a spec as callable tools, with authentication such as API key or managed identity, so the agent can use them reliably.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: What is the code interpreter tool used for in an agent?

options.A: Translating source code from Python into the Java language for deployment
options.B: Checking the agent's code for spelling mistakes in comments
options.C: Installing operating system updates on the machine that hosts the agent
options.D: Running model-written Python in a sandbox for analysis, calculations and charts

questions.explanation: Code interpreter executes Python in an isolated environment, so an agent can compute results and produce files or charts instead of guessing numbers.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: How can an indexer avoid reprocessing every document each time it runs against a SQL data source?

options.A: By using a change detection policy such as a high water mark column
options.B: By setting the number of replicas to zero before every run
options.C: By deleting and recreating the data source before every scheduled run
options.D: By running the indexer only during a leap year

questions.explanation: Change detection policies let indexers pick up only new or modified rows. Recreating sources or removing replicas does not identify changes.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: An indexed source row is deleted in the data source. How can Azure AI Search remove its document from the index?

options.A: By configuring a deletion detection policy, such as a soft delete column
options.B: By waiting for the search service to notice that a row is missing on its own
options.C: By changing the semantic ranker so it hides documents that were deleted
options.D: By increasing the number of partitions until old documents are pushed out

questions.explanation: Indexers cannot see that a row has vanished unless a deletion detection policy, for example a soft-delete marker column, tells them which documents to remove.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: What is the purpose of index projections in an Azure AI Search skillset?

options.A: To predict how many queries the index will receive during the next billing month
options.B: To display a live preview of the index on a projector in a meeting room for the team
options.C: To convert the whole index into a spreadsheet file that people can download
options.D: To turn each enriched chunk into its own document in a secondary index, linked to its parent

questions.explanation: Index projections let a single source document produce many chunk documents in an index, which is the usual shape for RAG, while keeping a link to the parent document.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: How can Azure AI Search apply security trimming so users see only documents they are allowed to read?

options.A: Hide the search endpoint and tell users not to search for restricted words
options.B: Store group or user IDs on each document and filter every query by the caller's identity
options.C: Ask the model to ignore documents that the user should not see
options.D: Increase the replica count so that restricted documents are spread across servers

questions.explanation: Security filters on identifiers are applied by the search service before results are returned, which enforces access. Leaving it to the model or obscurity does not.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: What does a scoring profile in Azure AI Search allow you to do?

options.A: Boost the relevance of documents based on fields such as freshness or tags
options.B: Rate the quality of the network connection between the client and service
options.C: Measure the credit score of the company that owns the service
options.D: Give users a numeric score for how well they use the search portal

questions.explanation: Scoring profiles adjust how relevance is calculated, for example by boosting recent documents or particular categories, without changing the underlying content.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: The embedding model outputs 1,536 dimensions, but the vector field in the index is defined with 3,072 dimensions. What happens when documents are indexed?

options.A: The vectors are padded with random numbers and indexed without any error
options.B: The service switches to a different embedding model that produces 3,072 dimensions
options.C: Indexing fails or is rejected because vector length must match the field's dimensions
options.D: The search service automatically shrinks the field to 1,536 dimensions and continues

questions.explanation: The dimension setting in the field must equal the length of the vectors, so a mismatch causes errors instead of silent conversion.

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: When would you choose exhaustive KNN instead of HNSW for a vector field in Azure AI Search?

options.A: When the dataset contains billions of vectors that must be queried within milliseconds
options.B: When you want the index to use less storage than any other algorithm
options.C: When the vectors are stored in a different Azure Region from the service
options.D: When the dataset is small or you need exact nearest neighbors and can accept slower queries

questions.explanation: Exhaustive KNN compares against every vector and returns exact results, which suits small sets and testing. HNSW is an approximate method that scales better for large indexes.

options.D: Azure Database for PostgreSQL

questions.domain: Build RAG and knowledge-mining solutions
questions.question: What does a semantic configuration in Azure AI Search define?

questions.explanation: A semantic configuration identifies the fields the semantic ranker uses to understand each document, such as a title field and content fields.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: In an Azure OpenAI response, what does a finish_reason of content_filter indicate?

options.A: The generation was stopped or omitted because the content filter triggered
options.B: The model asked to call a function and is waiting for the result
options.C: The model completed the answer normally and reached its natural stopping point
options.D: The output was cut off because the maximum number of tokens was reached

questions.explanation: A content_filter finish reason tells the caller that filtering blocked or truncated the output, so the application can respond gracefully. The other reasons are stop, length and tool calls.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: What is the purpose of a safety system message, also called a metaprompt, in a generative AI application?

options.A: To store the user's password so that the model can sign in to services on their behalf
options.B: To replace the platform content filters so that they can be turned off entirely
options.C: To encrypt the conversation transcripts that are stored in the application database
options.D: To steer the model toward safe, on-scope behavior in addition to content filters

questions.explanation: System-level instructions steer the model toward safe, on-scope behavior. They complement but do not replace content filtering and other safeguards.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: Which Azure AI Content Safety capability analyzes uploaded pictures for harmful material?

options.A: The image analysis API, which returns harm category severities
options.B: The speech synthesis API, which creates voices from text
options.C: The text blocklist API, which matches only written words
options.D: The optical character recognition API, which only extracts text and never judges it

questions.explanation: Content Safety includes image analysis that assigns severity to categories such as violence and sexual content. Blocklists apply to text, and OCR alone does not evaluate harm.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A search-based app only queries an Azure AI Search index and never writes to it. Which role follows least privilege for its managed identity?

options.B: Search Index Data Contributor
options.C: Search Service Contributor
options.D: Search Index Data Reader

questions.explanation: Search Index Data Reader allows read queries against index data. Contributor and Owner roles add write or management permissions the application does not need.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI
questions.question: A search service is reached through a private endpoint, but clients cannot resolve its name to the private IP address. What is missing?

options.A: A larger virtual machine size for each of the search service replicas in use

options.C: A public IP address that is assigned to each client computer in the virtual network
options.D: A private DNS zone linked to the virtual network so the service name resolves privately

questions.explanation: Private endpoints need DNS records, typically in a linked private DNS zone, so that the service hostname maps to the private IP within the network.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI

questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI documentation states that customer data, including prompts and completions, is not used to train or improve the base models offered to others.

questions.domain: Implement content moderation, security, and responsible AI

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions

options.C: A manual reminder for an engineer to add servers each morning
options.D: A KEDA-based HTTP scaling rule with minimum and maximum replica counts

questions.explanation: Container Apps supports scale rules based on HTTP concurrency or other triggers, adding and removing replicas automatically within limits.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions

options.C: A dedicated GPU virtual machine that runs all day
options.D: A physical server in a colocation facility

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Which alert would give early warning that a provisioned Azure OpenAI deployment is nearing capacity?

options.A: An alert on the number of tags that are applied to the resource group
options.B: A metric alert on provisioned utilization or a rise in HTTP 429 responses
options.C: An alert on the color theme that is selected in the Azure portal

questions.explanation: Utilization and throttling metrics indicate that capacity is being exhausted, so alerts on them let teams react before users are affected.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: What is a benefit of deploying an updated App Service to a staging slot and then swapping it into production?

options.A: The swap deletes the old version permanently so that it can never be restored
options.B: The production site is switched off for a full day while the swap occurs
options.C: The new build is validated and warmed up before it takes traffic, with easy rollback
options.D: The staging slot automatically doubles the context window of the deployed model

questions.explanation: Slots let you test the new build in a production-like environment, swap with little downtime, and swap back if a problem appears.

questions.domain: Deploy, monitor, and optimize AI solutions
questions.question: Which two actions commonly lower the token cost of a multi-turn chat application without changing the model?

options.A: Add more few-shot examples to every prompt, and repeat the system message
options.B: Send each user message twice, and raise the temperature
options.C: Increase max tokens on every request, and disable all caching
options.D: Trim or summarize older conversation history, and keep prompts concise

questions.explanation: Input tokens include the resent history, so summarizing or trimming it and keeping instructions tight cuts cost. The other actions increase token usage.

questions.domain: Implement an agentic solution
questions.question: How can you observe an agent's steps, tool calls and latency in production in Azure AI Foundry?

options.A: Enable tracing with OpenTelemetry and send the traces to Application Insights
options.B: Ask the agent to describe its own steps in a later chat and trust its description
options.C: Read the deployed model's weights to see which tools it chose for each request
options.D: Turn on content filtering, which records each tool call in an audit trail automatically

questions.explanation: Agents can emit OpenTelemetry traces that show each step, tool call and its latency, and Application Insights stores and visualizes them. A model's own account of its steps is unreliable, and weights and content filters do not expose tool calls.
